title: Congressional division of labor and drafting conditions
shortTitle: Congressional division of labor and drafting conditions
summary: Congress produces legislation through committees, staff, leadership, professional drafters, floor proceedings, and negotiations between chambers.
notes:
This division of labor permits specialization and helps a large institution act under competing demands. It also creates multiple decision points where language can change, ambiguities can survive, and compromises can be recorded. Authorizations and appropriations perform different functions, while oversight supplies feedback about implementation.

Katzmann uses those features to explain why committee and conference materials matter to members who vote on legislation. He acknowledges that outside groups and late floor drafting can affect quality. The descriptive account explains how institutional purpose may be communicated; it does not establish that every report reliably represents every member or that legislative procedure cures all ambiguity.
